whatToWatch.text: Bounce-back road test: Seattle's 3-2 and coming off a loss, and Vegas still likes them as 2.5-point favorites in Denver. Win this one and the skid stops at one.

Low-scoring slugfest incoming: that 40.5 over/under says it all — Seattle's allowing 21 a game, Denver 22.2, and both lines are getting home (2.8 sacks per game for the Hawks, 2.6 for the Broncos). Every possession is going to feel enormous.

Injury report swings both ways: Drew Lock, Zach Charbonnet and Jaxon Smith-Njigba headline Seattle's report with one player out and four questionable — but Denver's down two, including corners Pat Surtain II and Riley Moss. If Surtain can't go, that's a different secondary to attack.

newsBlurb.text: Seattle heads to Denver on a short week for a Thursday nighter it's already calling critical, and the message out of the building is blunt: the Seahawks believe they can be great, but they've left too much on the field to prove it yet. Reinforcements arrive in the kicking game, where wideout Irv Charles comes off injured reserve and back onto the 53 after missing the season's opening stretch. Clean it up in the thin air, and the talk starts matching the tape.
